sections.content: How many people are "medical and dental technicians"?

32,585 people

were counted on the census as "medical and dental technicians" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Medical and dental technicians operate, calibrate and maintain cardiographic and encephalographic testing equipment, assist in the conduct of post mortems, give simple dental treatments, fit artificial limbs and hearing aids, and undertake a wide range of related medical and dental tasks.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "medical and dental technicians" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "medical and dental technicians", 14.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "medical and dental technicians" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "medical and dental technicians" included:

  • engineering professionals (other)
  • quality assurance technicians
  • telecoms and related network installers and repairers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "medical and dental technicians" there were more women than men (63.7% compared with 36.3%).

This means "medical and dental technicians" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health and social care associate professionals".

Men made up 36.3% and women made up 63.7% of "medical and dental technicians"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "medical and dental technicians" included:

  • pharmacists
  • call and contact centre occupations
  • sales and retail assistants

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "medical and dental technicians" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "medical and dental technicians" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "medical and dental technicians", 8.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (70.3% compared with 29.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (80.8%) than self-employed (19.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
